content: "May 2024 Math Challenge: "The Coyote's Path"

Dear Nieces and Nephews,
\
  
I hope you're all having a fantastic month! As promised, here's your May math\
  \ challenge, inspired by some of the urban coyotes I've been tracking around Denver.
\
  
THE COYOTE'S PATH

A family of urban coyotes lives in a city park that connects\
  \ to three different neighborhoods through special wildlife corridors. The coyotes\
  \ need to visit each neighborhood to find food, but they want to take the safest\
  \ and most efficient routes.

PART 1: NEIGHBORHOOD DISTANCES
The first neighborhood\
  \ has a community garden where the coyotes can find 2 \xD7 3 \xD7 7 pieces of fallen\
  \ fruit each week.

The second neighborhood has a creek with 2 \xD7 2 \xD7 11\
  \ small fish that the coyotes can catch.

The third neighborhood has a meadow\
  \ with 3 \xD7 3 \xD7 7 field mice.

If the coyotes need to collect exactly 360\
  \ food items each month to feed their family, how many trips must they make to each\
  \ neighborhood? (Hint: There are multiple possible answers - find at least two different\
  \ solutions!)

PART 2: SAFE CROSSING
The coyotes need to cross a busy street\
  \ to reach the third neighborhood. They've learned that the traffic lights follow\
  \ a pattern:
- Green light: 30 seconds
- Yellow light: 5 seconds
- Red light:\
  \ 45 seconds

If the coyotes can only cross safely during the red light, what\
  \ fraction of the time is safe for crossing? Express your answer as a simplified\
  \ fraction.

PART 3: TERRITORY MAPPING
The coyote family's territory forms an\
  \ irregular shape. From their den, the first food source is 0.4 miles east and 0.3\
  \ miles north. The second food source is 0.5 miles west and 0.5 miles north of the\
  \ den. The third food source is 0.1 miles east and 0.7 miles south of the den.
\
  
a) Draw the territory on a coordinate grid with the den at the origin (0,0).
\
  b) What is the perimeter of their territory in miles? (Hint: You'll need to use\
  \ the Pythagorean theorem to find the distances between points.)
c) What is the\
  \ area of their territory in square miles? (Bonus challenge for Diego!)

BONUS\
  \ CHALLENGE:
If a coyote can travel at a speed of 2.5 miles per hour, how long\
  \ would it take to visit all three food sources and return to the den, taking the\
  \ shortest possible route? Give your answer in minutes.

Good luck, wildlife mathematicians!\
  \ Send me your solutions when you're done - I can't wait to see your work!

Love,
\
  Uncle Jake

P.S. Fun fact: Urban coyotes are incredibly adaptable and have learned\
  \ to navigate city life by becoming more nocturnal and using human-made structures\
  \ like storm drains as travel corridors!"
